From b555912b9b21075e8298015f888ffe3ff60b1a97 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 13:12:30 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] rxrpc: Fix key parsing memleak

In rxrpc_preparse_xdr_yfs_rxgk(), the memory attached to token->rxgk can be
leaked in a few error paths after it's allocated.

Fix this by freeing it in the "reject_token:" case.

Fixes: 0ca100ff4df6 ("rxrpc: Add YFS RxGK (GSSAPI) security class")
Closes: https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260319150150.4189381-1-dhowells%40redhat.com
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
cc: Marc Dionne <marc.dionne@auristor.com>
cc: Jeffrey Altman <jaltman@auristor.com>
cc: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
cc: linux-afs@lists.infradead.org
cc: stable@kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260408121252.2249051-3-dhowells@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/rxrpc/key.c b/net/rxrpc/key.c
index af403f0ccab5..26d4336a4a02 100644
--- a/net/rxrpc/key.c
+++ b/net/rxrpc/key.c
@@ -274,6 +274,7 @@ static int rxrpc_preparse_xdr_yfs_rxgk(struct key_preparsed_payload *prep,
 nomem:
 	return -ENOMEM;
 reject_token:
+	kfree(token->rxgk);
 	kfree(token);
 reject:
 	return -EKEYREJECTED;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `net/rxrpc/key.c`

- **Change**: Added `kfree(token->rxgk);` before `kfree(token);` in the `reject_token:` error label of `rxrpc_preparse_xdr_yfs_rxgk()`.

### Relationship

In the function `rxrpc_preparse_xdr_yfs_rxgk()`, memory is allocated for both `token` and its member `token->rxgk` during parsing. Under certain error conditions (e.g., parsing failures), the code jumps to the `reject_token:` label where only `token` was freed, leaking the memory attached to `token->rxgk`. The added `kfree(token->rxgk)` ensures that the inner allocation is freed before the outer `token` structure is freed, eliminating the memory leak. This fix targets the specific error path where `token->rxgk` was allocated but not properly released.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
token->rxgk = kzalloc(sizeof(*token->rxgk) + keylen, GFP_KERNEL);
</text>
<text>
goto reject_token;
</text>
<text>
reject_token:
	kfree(token);
</text>
Reason:
After `token->rxgk` is allocated, validation checks (e.g., for `level` or `enctype`) may fail and jump to the `reject_token` label. That label only frees `token` but not `token->rxgk`, causing the memory allocated to `token->rxgk` to be leaked. Other error paths (e.g., `nomem_yrxgk`, `expired`) correctly free `token->rxgk`, but `reject_token` does not.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
reject_token:
	kfree(token->rxgk);
	kfree(token);
</text>
Reason:
Adding `kfree(token->rxgk)` before `kfree(token)` in the `reject_token` label ensures that the memory allocated for `token->rxgk` is freed when a validation error occurs, preventing the memory leak.
